arbiter.summary: All 10 findings are CONFIRMED by the skeptic, in-scope of this diff, and reproduced against production validation code (not hypothetical). None qualify for decline under rule 2 - none are pre-existing baseline behavior, none are covered by a standing project disposition (the CLAUDE.md atomicity/config-getter/error-logging rules don't touch shell-parsing, JSON-validation, or AST-scanning gate logic), and none of the affected modules document the gap as an accepted residual (several explicitly claim to close exactly the gap the finding reopens, e.g. nonexec-delta.sh's own header vs index 3/4). Eight of ten fail toward SILENCE (an unaudited/unobserved change is accepted as clean), the worse failure direction per project standing rules; two (7, and partially 9) fail toward a human hitting a broken command or a stale credential, lower risk but still real. Index 6 (pairing-proof false PROVEN) is not speculative - the project's own CLAUDE.md bench inventory records a live instance (lane nq-c, 'Pairing PROVEN... before-read was unavailable') resting on exactly this hole. Index 8's skeptic-corrected severity (medium->high) is adopted: a silent exit-0 with no worker launched after 'start' is a lifecycle failure a human will not notice until the next unrelated check. No refutations were supplied to sanity-check, so unsound_refutations is empty by construction, not by judgment.

Its command word is `then`, which matches neither the `gh` arm nor the shell-runner list at :200-202, so the `*) echo NO` arm fires, the segment is never appended to $CMD_M, and the empty-$CMD_M grep at :277 returns 1 -> `exit 0` at :282. Measured with no marker present and ADVERSARIAL_MARKER_DIR empty: control `gh pr merge 424242` gave rc=2 from pre-merge-gate.sh and rc=2 from pre-merge-checks-gate.sh; the if/then form gave rc=0 from BOTH. The canary at pre-merge-gate.sh:110-115 passes (it probes the plain form), so nothing else catches it. Impact matches the claim: an unaudited merge allowed with no CI check either, since both gates share this one parser.

With no `gate` key, mark-audited.sh:117-120 checks only that `.findings` is an array and that its length is 0; nothing reads `error`, `codex_exit` or `unavailable`. codex-audit.sh documents exactly this shape for an infra failure (`{"findings":[], "error":"...", "codex_exit":N}`, codex-audit.sh:103) and its die_json merges $prov -- which carries head_sha (codex-audit.sh:229, provenance built at :425) -- so a timeout after SHA resolution produces an artifact naming the live head. Fed such an artifact (findings:[], error, codex_exit:124, unavailable:true, head_sha=live head), mark-audited.sh exited 0 and wrote the clearance marker. codex-audit.sh:191-193 itself warns "a consumer that only counts findings will read a quota failure as a clean audit" -- mark-audited.sh is that consumer.

confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced in a fresh scratch repo. nonexec-delta.sh:147 assigns `changed=$(git -C "$R" diff --name-status "$A" "$B")` with no status check, and :148 treats an empty value as proof: `[ -n "$changed" ] || { echo "PROVEN: no diff..."; exit 0; }`. The commit-identity guard at :146 does not help -- it uses rev-parse, which is unaffected, and passes the differing commits through. With `diff.orderFile=/nonexistent/orderfile` set, `git diff --name-status` exits 128 with empty stdout; nonexec-delta.sh then printed `PROVEN: no diff` and exited 0 across a commit that modified an executable file. End-to-end: `mark-audited.sh feat --audit <PASS artifact at A> --head <B> --carry-forward-from <A>` took that exit 0 at mark-audited.sh:154-155 as proof and wrote the marker (`carriedFrom=<A>`), carrying an old PASS onto unaudited executable code. Same fail-open shape also present at :106 for the CHANGED_PY probe.

confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced end to end against the pinned commit 09b532a. The pre-filter at nonexec-delta.sh:117 admits the file (src contains "getdoc"), but every arm of the AST walk then misses a bare-name call: nonexec-delta.sh:125 matches only ast.Attribute whose .attr is __doc__/getdoc/render_doc, so `from inspect import getdoc; getdoc(mod)` is an ast.Call(func=ast.Name(id='getdoc')) and matches nothing; :127 wants the literal string "__doc__"; :129 matches only a Call to Name 'help'; :131 matches only a bare Name '__doc__'. ast.ImportFrom/ast.alias is never inspected. Repro: main.py = `from inspect import getdoc; import mod; print(getdoc(mod))`, mod.py docstring changed 'old output' -> 'new output'. Application output changes (verified: old prints 'old output', new prints 'new output'), while the scanner printed `ok M mod.py (docstrings/comments only; ASTs identical)` then `PROVEN: ...touches no executable line`, rc=0 -- i.e. a stale audit is carried forward onto a behavioural change, which is the exact defect the file's own header (lines 47-50) claims to close. Note the attribute form `inspect.getdoc(mod)` IS caught at :125; only the imported bare-name form evades, which is why I rate this medium rather than high.

confirmed.title: Staged test deletions are resurrected in mutation copies
confirmed.failure_scenario: Commit mod.py with f() returning 1, test_guard.py asserting that result, and an unrelated passing smoke test. Run git rm test_guard.py, then mutate 'return 1' to 'return 2' with unittest discovery. The clone restores test_guard.py from HEAD, the overlay omits it, and git ls-files --deleted does not list its staged deletion. The restored test kills the mutant, so the tool reports KILLED even though the actual working suite no longer tests the guard.

confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced exactly as described. The clone at mutate.sh:183 (`git clone --local`) restores HEAD's working tree; the overlay at :206 uses `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, and after `git rm test_guard.py` the path is in neither the index nor the untracked set, so the overlay omits it; the deletion sweep at mutate.sh:215 uses `git ls-files --deleted`, which lists index entries missing from the working tree -- `git rm` removes the index entry too, so it lists nothing. Measured: `git ls-files --deleted` output was empty, the real working suite ran 1 test and passed (the guard is gone), and mutate.sh nevertheless reported `KILLED: baseline green (rc=0), mutant red (rc=1)` with the failure traceback pointing at `/tmp/.../run-mutant/test_guard.py` -- the resurrected file. The comment on :214 ("a file deleted in the working tree must not reappear from HEAD") states the property the line fails to deliver for the staged-deletion case. Impact is a harness-manufactured verdict certifying that a test catches a defect when that test is no longer in the suite -- the same class mutate.sh:169-172 records as critical, in the false-KILLED direction. The 'lines the mutation ADDED' diagnostic does print test_guard.py, but it warns about a multi-effect mutation, not about a resurrected file, so it does not dispose the finding.

confirmed.failure_scenario: Wire the registered PICkit to board B while the registered COM port belongs to board A. Board A answers both identity queries with the same serial, its first capabilities query times out, and its second returns its unchanged firmware CRC. Flashing B reports success. Because before_crc is empty, the comparison is skipped and the script reports PROVEN for the incorrect pairing. Reproduced the final decision with these values.

confirmed.reasoning: Traced and replayed the decision block verbatim. With before_crc empty, after_crc non-empty, and the same serial on both reads, the guard at pairing-proof.sh:129 is short-circuited by its own `[ -n "$before_crc" ]` conjunct, :126 passes, :113 is not entered, and :133 prints PROVEN with rc=0 -- no firmware change was ever observed, which is the one thing the script exists to observe (header lines 5-12). Reachability is high and not hypothetical: crc() at :68-69 yields empty on a single 6000 ms timeout, a transient read failure, or firmware predating CONF:CAP:JSON?, with no retry at all (contrast idn(), retried 5x at :106). The project CLAUDE.md bench inventory records an actual instance -- lane nq-c, 'Pairing PROVEN 2026-09-10 (crc32 unreadable -> 9CF57ADD, identity unchanged; the before-read was unavailable...)' -- a PROVEN verdict already resting on the after-read alone. The warning at :86 ('the proof will rest on the after-read alone') names the hole rather than disposing it: an after-read alone cannot distinguish 'the write landed on this board' from 'this board was never touched', so the script reports PROVEN for a mis-wired pairing, re-enabling the false-bisect failure its header cites from 2026-07-15 and 2026-08-24.

contributions.failure_scenario: Register the documented PICkit 5 serial 020026703RYN079002 on a lane and generate its brief. render_brief accepts only BUR-prefixed programmer serials, so it emits 'PICkit 4 serial <none>' and instructs the worker to pass --ts <none>. confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced. lane.sh:70 is `pk=$(grep -oE '\bBUR[0-9]+\b' <<<"$row" | head -1)`, which cannot match the documented PICkit 5 serial 020026703RYN079002 (no BUR prefix, contains R/Y/N). Ran the three greps from lane.sh:68-70 against a registry row `nq-b COM8 <16-hex> 020026703RYN079002`: port=[COM8], sn=[<16-hex>], pk=[<none>]. The `${pk:-<none>}` substitution at lane.sh:74 then renders brief.template.md:18 as 'PICkit 4 serial **<none>**. Always pass `--ts <none>` to `flash.sh`.' -- wrong programmer family plus no selector. Following it verbatim fails as claimed: `bash -c 'flash.sh --ts <none>'` gives `syntax error near unexpected token 'newline'` (`<none>` parses as redirections). The sibling file in this same change states the invariant being violated -- pairing-proof.sh:46-49: 'The programmer serial has no fixed shape: a PICkit 4 reads like BUR184882598, a PICkit 5 like 020026703RYN079002. Do not pattern-match it' -- and that script derives the family from the USB PID instead (:54-64). The affected lane is real: CLAUDE.md's bench inventory registers nq-b with PICkit 5 020026703RYN079002, and records that -TS is mandatory with two PICkits attached while -TP does not fall back across families. Rated medium rather than high because the failure is loud (a syntax error, not a flash of the wrong board) and the rendered '<none>' is visible to the reader of the brief.

confirmed.title: Starting a stopped Orca lane never recreates its terminal
confirmed.failure_scenario: Run lane.sh up nq-a, lane.sh down nq-a, then lane.sh start nq-a using Orca. down closes the terminal and saves TERMINAL as empty. start immediately sends to that empty handle without calling orca_terminal, then repeats failed sends and eventually exits 0. The documented restart sequence launches no worker.

contributions.title: Starting a stopped Orca lane never recreates its terminal
contributions.failure_scenario: Run lane.sh up nq-a, lane.sh down nq-a, then lane.sh start nq-a using Orca. down closes the terminal and saves TERMINAL as empty. start immediately sends to that empty handle without calling orca_terminal, then repeats failed sends and eventually exits 0. The documented restart sequence launches no worker.

confirmed.reasoning: cmd_down (lane/lane.sh:258-260) clears TERMINAL and persists the state file; cmd_start (line 215) only load_states and its orca arm calls orca_send directly at line 220 — orca_terminal is called only from cmd_up (line 204). orca_send discards status (>/dev/null 2>&1, no || check) and the script is set -uo pipefail without -e, so the empty --terminal send fails silently; terminal wait warns, both resend attempts fail, and the loop's final `[ "$attempt" = 2 ] && echo ...` returns 0 so the script exits 0 with no agent launched. The restart sequence is documented in lane/SKILL.md line 11 ('(re)launch the agent') and line 76 ('after a restart, lane.sh start <lane> re-arms it'). herdr backend is unaffected since PANE survives down.

confirmed.title: Removing a YAML credential field leaves verification falsely clean
confirmed.failure_scenario: Import google-ads.yaml containing refresh_token, then remove that field or set it to null while retaining the file. desired() omits the key, and stale detection checks only wholly absent source files. Import succeeds without flagging the retained credential; verify returns 0 with '0 problem(s)' and labels the key merely extra. Restore subsequently recreates the removed refresh_token from the vault. Reproduced the verifier's false-clean result.

confirmed.reasoning: With the source YAML still present, a removed key (or `key: null`, skipped at bws/bws-box.py:96-97) is simply absent from want, while desired() adds nothing to `absent` because the file exists (lines 111-115). _stale_for_absent (129-140) iterates only `absent`, so no stale key is reported. cmd_verify therefore has empty `bad`, prints '0 problem(s)', classifies the retained vault key as `extra` at line 202 ('not produced by this box') and returns 0 (line 208). cmd_import's stale branches are likewise unreachable (line 151 walks absent; line 153 needs the key present-but-empty in want). cmd_restore's YAML reassembly (lines 224-243) then writes every GOOGLE_ADS_* vault key back into the file, recreating the deleted refresh_token. Field-level removal is a real gap; only whole-file deletion is covered.
